relevance_note: The paper describes five Tangier disease patients from one Greek family, including the proband: 'DNA analysis revealed a new null mutation (C2033A) in both alleles'.
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; a short Python script assembled the JSON and sliced the Table 1 row segments (checked against the table). Labels: 'Case 1'-'Case 5' are the paper's own labels (Results also call them 'patient 1'-'patient 5'; pedigree labels V10, V9, V16, V17, V14). The parents IV4 and IV5 are included as relatives described in relation to the proband (figure legend: 'obligate heterozygotes'); they have no variant rows because no variant is printed for them and they were not tested. Only Case 1 was genotyped (C2033A, homozygous). For Cases 2-5 the authors write 'we assume that the C2033A mutation is probably present in each case. However, further studies are required to confirm this assumption'; HTD/hTD for them is a lipid-based diagnosis, so no variant rows were created for Cases 2-5 (abstention). The variant string 'C2033A' is not in c. notation, so cdna_hgvs is null; protein given only as 'premature stop codon at the amino acid residue 573'. Low HDL cholesterol (all five) and low apo A-I (Cases 1-3) are recorded as observed from Table 1 values against the control mean (HDL-C 1.3, Apo A1 3.8); apo A-I for Cases 4-5 (1.9, 2.6) left not reported as the paper does not characterise them. Table 1 prints ',0.5' (apparently '<0.5') for Apo A1 in Cases 2-3; copied as printed. No LDL values are given, so low LDL is not reported. 'No enlarged tonsils' (Cases 1-2) is narrower than the checklist item 'orange-colored or enlarged tonsils', which stays not reported for them; 'normal tonsils' (Cases 3-5) is recorded as excluding it. Case 1 'No ... atherosclerosis' is used to exclude both atherosclerotic checklist items. Normal whole investigations (Case 2 neurological examination, Case 3 blood tests, echocardiography for all five) are recorded as written and exclude nothing more specific. Group statements naming 'All five patients' (echocardiography, ECG/exercise tests; 'They had normal arterial blood pressures and fasting glucose and were not obese') and 'The patients with hTD' (fasting TG) are recorded as inferred from group statement; normal fasting glucose does not settle the broader checklist item on glucose intolerance. Smoking status was not recorded as a feature. No contradictions found; the abstract's 'high fasting TG' for two HTD patients matches the Results ('mild hypertriglyceridaemia', patients 2 and 3). The 25 controls are not in scope. Pedigree ages are in figure 1, which is not available as text.
